parent_claim_text: Economic concentration can weaken democratic accountability.
parent_status: NOT ENOUGH EVIDENCE — preserved historical umbrella
rule: Do not mutate CC-CLAIM-003 claim_text in this slice. Create falsifiable modules. Public reasoning explains why the umbrella claim fails.

modules.title: Economic resource concentration
modules.proposed_wording: U.S. household wealth and selected industry market structures show high concentration at the top of their distributions.
modules.notes: Already largely covered by CC-CLAIM-011/005 — module exists to stop smuggling concentration into 'accountability'.

modules.title: Unequal policy responsiveness
modules.proposed_wording: Under some research designs, U.S. national policy outcomes associate more strongly with affluent and organized-business preferences than with average-citizen preferences when those preferences diverge; the magnitude and causal interpretation remain contested.
modules.notes: Gilens/Page + Branham/Soroka/Wlezien — association/contested causation, not capture.

modules.title: Campaign finance and lobbying disclosure (descriptive)
modules.proposed_wording: Federal campaign-finance and lobbying disclosure systems make large flows of political money and lobbying activity publicly observable; disclosure alone does not establish that economic concentration weakens democratic accountability.

modules.title: Regulatory capture (sectoral)
modules.proposed_wording: In specific regulated sectors, industry actors can systematically shape the agencies that regulate them; such capture must be evidenced sector-by-sector and is not established by national concentration statistics alone.

modules.title: State capture (systemic)
modules.proposed_wording: Private actors can, under some conditions, shape the formation of laws and rules to their advantage on a systemic basis; whether U.S. national politics meets a state-capture standard is not established by current Constitutional Capitalism sources.
modules.notes: Do not promote without identification standards.

recommendation_for_parent: Keep CC-CLAIM-003 as NEE umbrella OR retire/rewrite after ChatGPT governance choosing among modules A–E. Do not upgrade Supports.
